findings.title: Prod uptime monitor has not run since 2026-10-28T21:11Z; its last run misread HTTP 429 as an outage and could not send the alert
findings.evidence: The deployment's logs show a probe every 5 min up to 2026-10-28T21:05Z ('[uptime] ok ... -> 200'). At 21:11Z all three attempts got 429 from https://inventory.recycleservers.com/api/health. The origin answered 200, so the script printed 'prod DOWN ... Failing layer: Cloudflare edge/Worker/custom-domain'. The alert POST to the relay also got 'curl: (22) ... 429' ('[uptime] alert post failed'), the run exited 1 and Railway marked the deployment CRASHED. There are no deploy logs for this deployment from 21:11Z on 10-28 to 20:30Z on 10-31. Every later deployment (18:06Z to 20:14Z on 10-31, from dev pushes) is SKIPPED by watchPatterns, and list-deployments status=SUCCESS returns nothing. get-service-config shows no cronSchedule in the live deploy config and no configFile, so the schedule depended on railway.toml being picked up at deploy time.
findings.failure_scenario: Prod goes down (as on 2026-07-12) and nobody hears about it: the only probe of the public hostname is not running, and Railway's own dashboards stay green when only the Cloudflare layer breaks. It has been in this state for about 3 days. When it does run, a Cloudflare rate-limit (429) on Railway's shared egress IP raises a false 'DOWN, redeploy the Worker' alert, and the same rate-limit blocks that alert from reaching the relay.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner: restore the cron (redeploy uptime-monitor so railway.toml's cronSchedule applies, or set the schedule in service settings, then confirm that runs resume). Code: treat 429 and other non-5xx answers apart from real outages (retry with backoff, report 'rate-limited' rather than 'DOWN'), and add a dead-man's switch: the relay or another cron alerts when no uptime heartbeat has arrived in 15 min.
findings.regression_test: Stub-curl test for check.sh: 429x3 must not report the Worker domain as broken, and a 5xx with origin 200 still alerts. Watchdog check: if no '[uptime] ok' line in 15 min, raise an alert.

findings.title: One credential can both read and delete every prod DB backup; no object lock or versioning, and the R2 keys were in the 2026-10-21 Railway env exposure
findings.location: backup/backup.sh:97-111; backup/Dockerfile:15; infra/terraform/environments/experiment-backups/main.tf:33-36,54-61,96-104; docs/backups-cloud-runbook.md:11-17; Railway pg-r2-backup (3224fca5-f6cc-47f9-8dba-6b1db81fda1c) vars R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
findings.evidence: backup.sh prunes with `rclone deletefile`, so the job's single R2 key must have delete rights on recycle-db-backup. That bucket is not managed by Terraform: experiment-backups manages an unused 'recycle-erp-backups' bucket. There is no bucket lock, no versioning and no prevent_destroy. The runbook (last touched at v1.193.0, RS-134) lists all of these as 'still to make'. Live logs show nightly runs succeed and prune (e.g. 2026-10-31T03:30Z, 'Pruning old R2 backup: recycle_erp_railway_20261001T033452Z.dump.gz'), so the delete permission is live. Owner notes from 2026-10-23 list 'R2 x3' as not yet rotated after Railway's 2026-10-21 disclosure that customer env vars were read. Only names were inspected, so current rotation status is unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone holding the leaked or still-unrotated backup key can download all 30 full prod dumps (customers, orders, financials) and then delete them. A compromised Railway env or bad run can also prune every dump. Either way, no offsite copy is left for the next data-loss incident.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner: confirm or rotate the backup R2 key now. Then work through runbook steps 1-3: import recycle-db-backup into Terraform with prevent_destroy; give the cron a PutObject-only token and set BACKUP_KEEP=0 so the bucket lifecycle (30 d) handles retention; enable an R2 bucket lock with retention of at least 30 days.
findings.regression_test: After the change, a DeleteObject with the cron's token returns 403. Run terraform plan on experiment-backups: it shows the lock and lifecycle on recycle-db-backup and no drift.

findings.title: Merging to main deploys the prod backend (and runs its migrations) without waiting for CI; no branch protection requires a check
findings.location: Railway backend service 26d2f448-d4f2-4f67-b2ef-1628ef27a5c0 source.checkSuites=false (production/main and dev/dev); GitHub branch protection main+dev required_status_checks=null; .github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:11-13; apps/backend/Dockerfile:68
findings.evidence: `gh api .../branches/main/protection` and `.../dev/protection` both return required_status_checks: null. Railway get-service-config shows checkSuites: false for both environments. Release PR #1028 merged at 18:54:10Z, 3 s after its backend-tests 'test' run started (18:54:07Z). That run finished at 19:01:41Z, but Railway prod deployment 26e2ba24 (fb4afda4) was created at 18:54:13Z. The container CMD runs migrate.mjs before the server starts. backend-tests.yml's header says branch protection keys on the check name, but no such rule exists. deploy-frontend now gates the Worker on its own verify job (INF-01), but the backend side has no equivalent.
findings.failure_scenario: A release whose main merge ref fails typecheck or the backend suite (a hotfix on main that dev lacks, a bad merge resolution, or a PR merged while red) deploys to prod anyway. Its migrations run against the prod database before anyone sees the red check, and migrations cannot be rolled back.
findings.proposed_fix: Add required status checks on main and dev (backend-tests / test, version-check / version-tag-check, deploy-frontend / verify where it applies) with strict up-to-date. Turn on Railway 'Wait for CI' (checkSuites) for backend prod and dev. Correct the backend-tests.yml comment.
findings.regression_test: Throwaway PR to a scratch branch with a deliberately failing test: GitHub refuses the merge, and Railway shows the deployment WAITING until checks pass.

findings.title: [cross-lane] Nightly prod-to-dev db-sync has failed every night since 2026-10-28, with no alert
findings.location: deploy/railway-sync/scrub.sql:32-45 (generic *_enc nulling); apps/backend/migrations/0213_fleet_proxies.sql:14 (url_enc TEXT NOT NULL); deploy/railway-sync/sync.sh:111-116; Railway dev db-sync 006cd405-7bee-4a66-8ebc-6ca6fdaa44ad deployment 5fecc5a6 (status SUCCESS)
findings.evidence: db-sync logs: 10-25, 10-26 and 10-27 end '[sync] done'. On 10-28, 10-29, 10-30 and 10-31 each run fails with 'ERROR: null value in column "url_enc" of relation "fleet_proxies" violates not-null constraint', with context 'UPDATE public.fleet_proxies SET url_enc = NULL WHERE url_enc IS NOT NULL'. scrub.sql nulls every column matching '_enc$', and migration 0213 added url_enc as NOT NULL. The restore is one transaction, so dev is rolled back unchanged (safe), but the deployment still shows SUCCESS. tests/sync-scrub.test.ts seeds no fleet_proxies row, so the UPDATE touches nothing in CI and the bug never shows there.
findings.failure_scenario: Dev stays frozen at the 2026-10-27 prod copy. Data-migration dry runs and QA on dev then test against a stale schema and data shape while everyone assumes it refreshes nightly. The failure is visible only in logs.
findings.proposed_fix: Have scrub.sql delete rows (or set a placeholder) for NOT NULL *_enc columns, e.g. DELETE FROM fleet_proxies or skip attnotnull columns and handle them explicitly. Make a failed sync raise an alert through the relay's /alert route.
findings.regression_test: In sync-scrub.test.ts, seed a fleet_proxies row with url_enc set and assert that scrub.sql runs and leaves no sealed proxy URL behind.

findings.title: Prod backend watch patterns leave out root manifests, unlike dev; neither environment watches pnpm-workspace.yaml
findings.location: Railway backend production build.watchPatterns=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**]; dev=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.base.json]; pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-21; .github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:36-43
findings.evidence: get-service-config shows the two environments' patterns differ. Dependency security fixes in this repo land as overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml plus a lockfile change only (the exceljs>uuid and brace-expansion overrides). backend-tests.yml already treats those root files as backend-affecting.
findings.failure_scenario: A lockfile- or override-only security fix (e.g. a nodemailer refresh, see A11-09) merges to main. Prod backend is not rebuilt and keeps the vulnerable dependency until some unrelated backend change triggers a deploy. Dev, which watches the lockfile, gets the fix, so a check on dev wrongly suggests prod has it too.
findings.proposed_fix: Set the same watch patterns on both environments, matching backend-tests' list: apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, .npmrc, .nvmrc.
findings.regression_test: After the next override-only change, the deployment list shows a new prod backend build for that commit.

findings.title: The Worker behaviour test never gates a PR; it runs only after merge
findings.evidence: backend-tests triggers on deploy/cloudflare/** but never runs `tsx --test deploy/cloudflare/worker.test.mjs`. deploy-frontend runs it but has no pull_request trigger.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR that breaks the Worker's proxy, header or claim-env rules merges green. The post-merge verify job fails, so the dev Worker (or, on a release, the prod Worker) silently stops deploying while the backend side of that release goes out (A11-03), splitting the release.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the worker.test.mjs step to backend-tests (it is already on its path filter).
findings.regression_test: A PR that edits worker.js to drop X-Client-IP clearing fails backend-tests.

findings.title: Dependency gate is high-only and ERP-only; prod tree carries 6 moderate advisories; tracker dependency trees are never audited
findings.evidence: `pnpm audit --prod` (run 2026-10-31) found 0 high/critical and 6 moderate. Reachability of each: (1-3) nodemailer <10.1.4, three addressparser advisories; the fix is inside ^10, so a lockfile refresh is enough. Inbound mail headers come from the imapflow envelope and mailparser is used only for the body (src/mail/inbox.ts:166-177), so exposure is limited to parsing outbound recipient strings; not proven exploitable. (4) @hono/node-server serveStatic is unused in apps/backend/src, so unreachable. (5) ip-address via imapflow>socks, reachable only through a SOCKS proxy configuration. (6) minimatch via exceljs>archiver, which never sees user globs. The full tree's 19 highs are all devDependencies (vitest/vite/postcss/nanoid, workbox-build) and never ship. trackers/reddit audits at 6 moderate hono advisories (parseBody/serveStatic/jsx); api.ts uses c.req.json, so low reachability. The Facebook worker's pins (pip-audit 2.9.0) show diskcache 5.6.3 (PYSEC-2026-2447, pickle; needs write access to the cache directory) and filelock 3.32.7 (13 GHSAs, local attacker or Windows), both low reachability in a single-user container. The other five Python services pin only floors (fastapi>=0.110 and so on) and have no lock, so every image build resolves different versions.
findings.failure_scenario: A high advisory published against trackers/reddit's hono or the Facebook Python tree reaches nobody: no workflow audits either, and root CI is path-filtered away from trackers/. Moderates in the ERP prod tree also stay invisible indefinitely.
findings.proposed_fix: Refresh nodemailer to >=10.1.4. Add trackers/reddit and a pip-audit of worker-constraints.txt (and of locks to add for the five unpinned services) to the weekly dependency-audit run. Record moderate dispositions next to auditConfig.
findings.regression_test: Weekly dependency-audit run shows three jobs (ERP, reddit, facebook) green.

findings.title: version-check has no concurrency group; two quick dev pushes can tag a version on the wrong commit
findings.evidence: Nothing serializes version-tag-check on dev. Push A (bump to X) and push B (B rebased on A with no bump of its own) run at once. B sees LAST_TAG < X, passes, and tags vX on its own commit before A's job pushes; A's `git push origin vX` then fails. vX ends up on B's commit and covers code that never got a bump or changelog entry.
findings.failure_scenario: Two agents squash-merge within seconds (concurrent sessions are routine in this repo). The release tag and changelog then mislabel which code shipped, and fleet-images' 'already tagged on another commit' skip (fleet-images.yml:239-242) can build the agent image from the wrong commit.
findings.regression_test: Two quick pushes are queued one after the other; the second fails with 'Code changed since vX but package.json is still X'.

findings.title: The backend image's defaults fail open when NODE_ENV is missing
findings.evidence: The image bakes NODE_ENV=development, ENABLE_DEMO_ACCOUNTS=true, ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin and a published JWT_SECRET. Every production guard in env.ts keys on NODE_ENV === 'production'. Railway sets these variables today (names present on both environments).
findings.failure_scenario: Someone deletes or renames NODE_ENV on the Railway service (e.g. while rotating variables, as on 2026-10-22). The backend boots in development mode with every production refusal off (published JWT secret, missing PROXY_SECRET, stub OCR), and demo accounts are on if ENABLE_DEMO_ACCOUNTS was left at its default.
findings.proposed_fix: Default the image to NODE_ENV=production and leave secret defaults to docker-compose / the local .env. Or refuse to boot when RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT is set and NODE_ENV is not 'production'.
findings.regression_test: Unit test on buildEnv: RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT set, NODE_ENV unset, so it throws.

findings.title: Ops services drift from the release model and the docs
findings.location: Railway production uptime-monitor source.branch=dev; backup/README.md:3-4 and backup/railway.toml:1 (call the backup service 'db-sync'); Railway pg-r2-backup logs
findings.evidence: The production uptime-monitor deploys from dev, so a check.sh change reaches prod before any release (AGENTS.md: dev to main is the release). The backup docs name the service 'db-sync', but the live backup service is pg-r2-backup and db-sync is the prod-to-dev sync. Every backup run logs rclone's 'NOTICE: Config file ... not found' at error severity.
findings.failure_scenario: During an incident, an operator follows backup/README.md, opens db-sync and reads the wrong logs and settings. Every night's backup shows an error line that is not one, which teaches people to ignore real errors.
findings.proposed_fix: Point the uptime-monitor at main (or document it as an exception), fix the service name in the backup docs, and pass `--config /dev/null` or set RCLONE_CONFIG to silence the notice.
